chosen_property.label: occurredDuring
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the time period or event during which something happened.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures an event occurring during a time expression (period).

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: endDate

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime

candidates.label: scheduledTime

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. candidates.label: byDay

candidates.label: byMonthDay

candidates.label: deathDate

chosen_property.label: participant
chosen_property.justification: The 'participant' property is a general fit for entities involved in an action or event.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: The 'instrument' property correctly identifies the tool or means used in an action.

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: supply
candidates.comment: A resource relation between a how-to guide or direction and a consumable supply required for its execution. Also called "required supply", "consumable item", "material needed", "ingredient". Examples: "The recipe has supply flour", "The how-to direction requires supply glue", "This guide lists several supply items.". Distinct from tool, which refers to a non-consumable instrument.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

chosen_property.label: result
chosen_property.justification: The 'result' property correctly links an action to its outcome or consequence.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: description

candidates.label: associatedArticle

candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: appearance

candidates.label: backstory

Examples: "Article 'Investigative Report' backstory 'The journalist spent months...'", "NewsArticle 'Exposed Scandal' backstory 'This article originated from a tip-off...'."

candidates.label: firstAppearance

Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: relatedLink

candidates.label: event

Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: serviceAudience
candidates.comment: The specific group of people or entities for whom a service is intended or eligible. Also called target audience, service recipients, eligible users. Examples: `Healthcare Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Seniors`, `Educational Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Students`, `Financial Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Small Businesses`.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

relations.definition: Indicates the stated cause or justification for an event or observation.
relations.embedding_query_text: cited as reason for: Indicates the stated cause or justification for an event or observation.

instances: Zelensky on insufficient Patriot supply -> Ballistic missiles not shot down

chosen_property.label: justifies
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the stated cause or justification for an event or observation.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of a statement or assessment justifying an event.

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Indicates the document or publication where information was released.
relations.embedding_query_text: published in: Indicates the document or publication where information was released.

instances: Zelensky on insufficient Patriot supply -> statement

chosen_property.label: publishedIn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the document or publication where information was released.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of a creative work being published within another creative work (document).

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: sdDatePublished
candidates.comment: The date when the structured data associated with a creative work was generated or published. Also called structured data publication date, metadata publish date, data generation date. Examples: `Article JSON-LD` sdDatePublished `2023-10-26`, `Recipe Structured Data` sdDatePublished `2023-09-15`, `Event Markup` sdDatePublished `2023-08-01`. Distinct from `datePublished`, which is the publication date of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: publisherImprint
candidates.comment: A publisher imprint relation between a creative work and the specific publishing division or imprint responsible for its release. Also called imprint of, published under imprint. Examples: "A comic book has a publisher imprint 'Vertigo Comics'.", "A novel has a publisher imprint 'Vintage Books'.", "A children's book has a publisher imprint 'Puffin Books'."

relations.definition: Indicates a request for actions or resolutions originating from a specific body or event.

chosen_property.definition: Indicates a request for actions or resolutions originating from a specific body or event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of a request for decisions originating from a specific event or body.

Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
candidates.comment: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of requesting support for a specific entity.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

candidates.label: potentialAction

Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: endorsers
candidates.comment: An endorsers relation between a diet and the people or organizations that support or recommend it. Also called "supporters", "advocates", "recommenders". Examples: "Diet 'Mediterranean Diet' endorsers 'World Health Organization'", "Diet 'Vegan Diet' endorsers 'PETA'", "Diet 'Keto Diet' endorsers 'Dr. X'". Distinct from endorsee, which is the entity being supported.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
candidates.comment: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."

candidates.label: actionApplication
candidates.comment: An action application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software. Examples: "A 'send email' entry point's action application is 'Gmail'.", "A 'edit document' entry point's action application is 'Microsoft Word'." Distinct from application, which is a more general property for an application that can complete the request.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: actionOption
candidates.comment: An action option relation between a choose action and the available choices or alternatives. Also called choice alternatives, selection options, available choices. Examples: "A 'choose color' action's action option is 'red'.", "A 'select size' action's action option is 'large'."

relations.definition: Indicates an action or situation that provides incentive or support for another action.
relations.embedding_query_text: encourages: Indicates an action or situation that provides incentive or support for another action.

chosen_property.label: encourages
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an action or situation that provides incentive or support for another action or entity.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of one entity encouraging another.

candidates.label: incentivizedItem
candidates.comment: An incentivized item relation between a financial incentive and the product or service it encourages. Also called target item, promoted product, incentivized service. Examples: "A financial incentive applies to an incentivized item 'solar panels'.", "The rebate is for an incentivized item category.", "This incentive targets a specific incentivized item."

candidates.label: incentives
candidates.comment: An incentives relation between a job posting and a description of its bonus and commission compensation. Also called job bonuses, compensation package, additional pay. Examples: "A job posting includes incentives for performance.", "The role offers various incentives.", "This job has incentives described in the posting.". Distinct from incentiveCompensation, which is a more specific property for bonus and commission.

candidates.label: incentiveAmount
candidates.comment: An incentive amount relation between a financial incentive and the value that can be redeemed. Also called incentive value, redeemable amount, benefit amount. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive amount of $500.", "The incentive offers an incentive amount as a percentage.", "This incentive provides an incentive amount as a loan."

candidates.label: incentiveStatus
candidates.comment: An incentive status relation between a financial incentive and its current operational status. Also called status of incentive, incentive condition, program status. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive status 'active'.", "The program's incentive status is 'on hold'.", "This incentive has a retired incentive status."

candidates.label: incentiveType
candidates.comment: An incentive type relation between a financial incentive and the specific type of incentive offered. Also called type of benefit, incentive category, subsidy type. Examples: "A financial incentive has an incentive type 'tax credit'.", "The program offers an incentive type 'rebate'.", "This incentive is a 'subsidy' incentive type."

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: incentiveCompensation
candidates.comment: An incentive compensation relation between a job posting and a description of its bonus and commission aspects. Also called bonus structure, commission details, performance pay. Examples: "A job posting has incentive compensation details.", "The job offers incentive compensation based on sales.", "This role includes incentive compensation.". Distinct from incentives, which is a more general description of incentives.

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier
candidates.comment: An eligible with supplier relation between a financial incentive and the organization that supplies the incentivized item or service. Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

chosen_property.label: aimsToVanquish
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an objective or goal to defeat or overcome an entity.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures the concept of aiming to defeat or overcome an entity.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: secondaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A preventative therapy or intervention aimed at preventing the recurrence of a medical condition after an initial episode. Also called relapse prevention, post-episode prevention, reoccurrence therapy. Examples: `Heart Attack` secondaryPrevention `Aspirin Therapy`, `Stroke` secondaryPrevention `Lifestyle Modification: Diet and Exercise`, `Depression` secondaryPrevention `Medical Therapy: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy`. Distinct from `primaryPrevention`, which aims to prevent the *initial* occurrence.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: antagonist
candidates.comment: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: requirements

candidates.label: requiresSubscription

Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: valueRequired
candidates.comment: A value required relation between a property value specification and whether the property must be filled to complete an action. Also called mandatory field, required property, input necessity. Examples: "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'true'", "PropertyValueSpecification valueRequired 'false'", "Form field valueRequired 'true'".

candidates.label: competencyRequired
candidates.comment: A requirement relation for an educational credential or learning resource, specifying the knowledge, skill, or ability needed. Also called "required skill", "prerequisite competency", "learning outcome". Examples: "Certification competencyRequired 'Problem-solving skills'", "Course learning resource competencyRequired 'Basic algebra'".

candidates.label: coursePrerequisites
candidates.comment: A requirement relation between a course and the conditions or prior knowledge needed to take it. Also called: prerequisites, required courses, entry requirements. Examples: "Advanced Algorithms" course prerequisites "Data Structures", "Calculus II" course prerequisites "Calculus I", "Graduate Seminar" course prerequisites "permission of instructor".

candidates.label: dependencies
candidates.comment: A prerequisite relation between a tech article and the requirements needed to fulfill its steps. Also called: technical requirements, prerequisites, required components. Examples: "Software Installation Guide" dependencies "Python 3.8, pip", "Hardware Setup Article" dependencies "Screwdriver, Internet connection", "Programming Tutorial" dependencies "Basic understanding of algorithms".

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires.
